title: Characterization of valid configuration codes
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and let $C,n,s$ be natural numbers such that $C$ is at least the number of states plus $6$ times the number of work tapes plus $5$. For every Boolean word $w$ of length $C(s+n+1)$, the configuration-validity CNF formula evaluates to true when variable $j$ is assigned the bit of $w$ at position $j$ (and false beyond the word) if and only if there are a Boolean input string $x$ of length $n$ and a configuration $c$ on $x$, with all work-tape heads within distance $s$ of the origin and all work-tape cells outside that window blank, such that $w$ is the configuration code of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is at least the number of states plus $6$ times the number of work tapes plus $5
